scope: Synchronized real-scene versus rendered robot-execution comparison
summary: A ten-second 2x2 comparison now shows the unchanged real kitchen observation beside rendered pour, shake, and handover robot effects.
evidence: The published video decodes all 240 frames at 1664x960, 24 FPS, and ten seconds.
Five-point visual review covers frames 0, 60, 120, 180, and 239; all four synchronized panels remain present and labeled.
Each robot panel and the footer explicitly say simulated or no physical robot claim.
lessons: A synchronized multi-action grid makes source-to-render differences easier to inspect without selectively presenting one favorable action.
limitations: The robot panels are rendered counterfactuals, not footage of physical robot execution.
They are not inference from the one-step BWM smoke checkpoint.
Visual comparison does not establish causal action following, contact physics, safety, or task success.
next_actions: Use the separate calibrated telemetry-and-video protocol when physical robot access becomes available.
